thread:
alexc: Hey team, customer onacct-881 is reporting that embeddings from Hosted vs Dedicated are different shape and causing their indexer to crash. They call the embeddings API with the same payload and model name but get 1536 dims on Hosted and 1024 on Dedicated.

mariag: Ugh. Do we have the exact API calls and model param they used? often routing picks different model variants if model param is fuzzy.

alexc: They pasted their curl, here's the important bit: `POST /v1/embeddings` body: `{"model":"open-embed-1","input":["hello world"]}`. They say both envs use the same API key and they used our hosted endpoint vs their dedicated endpoint (dedicated url).

timr: Did they pin to a specific model version on Dedicated? If dedicated has an older model catalog it might map `open-embed-1` -> `open-embed-legacy-1024`.

mariag: Good point. @timr can you check the customer's Dedicated config for model alias mappings? Also ask them for the raw content-length/response headers from both calls.

ops-bot: Automated note: created support ticket #SUP-6621 and assigned to eng-oncall.

eng-oncall: I'm on it. Quick repro steps I asked the customer to run: 1) curl hosted `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings` with their hosted key, 2) curl dedicated `https://dedicated.customer.example/v1/embeddings` with their dedicated key, 3) include `--verbose` and save both responses as `hosted.json` and `dedicated.json`.

mariag: Also asked them to add `model_version` field if available and to try the canonical model id from our model catalog (e.g., `open-embed-1536-v2`).

alexc: Customer provided hosted.json and dedicated.json. Hosted shows: `{"data":[{"embedding":[...1536 numbers...] }], "model":"open-embed-1536-v2"}`. Dedicated response: `{"data":[{"embedding":[...1024 numbers...] }], "model":"open-embed-1024-q"}`.

timr: Aha — dedicated routed to a quantized 1024 variant. That explains dims. But why would dedicated accept `open-embed-1` and map it to a different canonical model? There should be alias resolution but it should be consistent.

mariag: Two possibilities: 1) Dedicated customer's deployment has a local model alias map that resolves `open-embed-1` to the 1024 variant. 2) Smart routing fallback chose a lower-cost model under heavy load. Which is more likely?

eng-oncall: For Dedicated, smart routing isn't supposed to change canonical model unless configured by the customer's routing policy. Check the customer's Dedicated config: `model_aliases.yaml` or the console UI mappings. I pulled their config — they had a pre-prod migration where `open-embed-1` was aliased to `open-embed-1024-q` to save cost during test. That explains it.

alexc: Customer says they never intended that alias. They used a reference integration that passed the alias. Need to advise rollback. Also they reported throughput differences: Hosted does 300 req/s, Dedicated peaked at 80 req/s.

mariag: Different throughput can be due to different GPU types and batching config. Dedicated likely has smaller pool + default batching disabled. Ask for Dedicated pool size and `batching.max_batch_size`, `batching.enabled` flags.

eng-oncall: I checked their Dedicated config: pool=2 gpus (A10G-equivalent), batching.enabled=false, and they have model variant `open-embed-1024-q` which is int8 quantized. That explains throughput and dim mismatch (model choice explains dim).

timr: Next steps for customer: 1) If they want parity with Hosted embeddings they should update Dedicated model alias to canonical `open-embed-1536-v2` and enable batching with `max_batch_size: 64` and `batch_window_ms: 8`. 2) Re-run and confirm dims. 3) If they need quantized variant still, update the indexer to accept 1024 dims or wrap a conversion step.

alexc: Customer also had auth errors intermittently when switching endpoints: `401` on Dedicated but only when hitting a certain LB. Might be token scoping difference between hosted keys and dedicated keys.

mariag: Remind them dedicated keys are endpoint-scoped; tokens aren't interchangeable. Also check clock skew if signed tokens.

eng-oncall: Action items I pushed to their console support plan: - Remove the unintended alias `open-embed-1` -> `open-embed-1024-q`. - Add canonical model mapping to `open-embed-1536-v2` for both hosted and dedicated to avoid ambiguity. - Turn on batching and adjust pool to 4 GPUs if they need 300 rps.

ops-bot: Note added to ticket #SUP-6621: suggested config changes and recommended next-step rollback.

mariag: For our docs team: we should add a KB article on "model alias mismatches across deployments" — this comes up a lot.

timr: Also a subtle repro tip: when verifying dims, include `--raw` binary save of the `embedding` array or checksum (e.g., sha256 of vector) because JSON pretty-printing can hide trailing zeros for some float formats.

alexc: Customer set up a test run after we suggested changes. They returned: after alias fix and enabling batching, both endpoints now return 1536 dims and indexer no longer crashes. Throughput improved to ~220 rps with pool=3 and batching window 10ms.

mariag: Great. Closing loop: documented recommended defaults for Dedicated embedding pools and added KB draft. Marking ticket resolved pending customer confirmation in 24h. :thumbsup: 

sre-bot: Incident telemetry: no platform-wide regression detected. This was configuration-specific.

alexc: Thanks everyone — customer happy. Will follow up if they want help resizing cluster.
